name: MonarchAiSuggestedActions
title: AiSuggestedActions
wrapsNative: VStack of rows with MonarchButton (Run, with isLoading), MonarchBadge tags and a ghost icon Button (dismiss), alert(_:isPresented:presenting:actions:message:) for approval, sensoryFeedback(.success/.error, trigger:) and AccessibilityNotification.Announcement
summary: The next best actions for a record, each with Run, an optional approval step and dismiss, and where the suggestions came from.
whenToUse: On a record screen (a customer, a ticket, a deal) to offer a few next steps an AI model or product rules suggest, which the person runs with one tap.
whenNotToUse: For approving a tool call an agent wants to make, with its arguments, use MonarchAiToolApproval. For follow-up prompts in a chat use MonarchAiFollowUpSuggestions. For a fixed set of record actions use the toolbar or a Menu.
api: init(_ actions: [MonarchAiSuggestedAction], title: String? = nil, origin: MonarchAiSuggestedActionsOrigin = .ai, labels: MonarchAiSuggestedActionsLabels = MonarchAiSuggestedActionsLabels(), onDismiss: (@MainActor (String) -> Void)? = nil, onRun: @escaping @MainActor (String) async throws -> Void)

public struct MonarchAiSuggestedAction: Identifiable, Sendable, Hashable { init(id: String, label: String, description: String? = nil, requiresApproval: Bool = false, risk: MonarchAiToolCallRisk = .low, consequences: [String] = [], confirmLabel: String? = nil, status: MonarchAiSuggestedActionStatus? = nil); var needsApproval: Bool { get } }
public enum MonarchAiSuggestedActionStatus: Sendable, Hashable, CaseIterable { case ready, running, done, failed }
public enum MonarchAiSuggestedActionsOrigin: Sendable, Hashable, CaseIterable { case ai, rule }

MonarchAiSuggestedActionsLabels.init(originAi:originRule:run:runAction:running:done:failed:dismiss:needsApproval:risk:approvalTitle:approvalDescription:approve:cancel:doneAnnouncement:empty:), every string String? = nil and every function (@Sendable (String) -> String)? = nil, risk (@Sendable (MonarchAiToolCallRisk) -> String?)? = nil

options.name: actions
options.description: The suggestions, most useful first: id, label, description, requiresApproval, risk, consequences, confirmLabel and an optional status.

options.name: origin
options.description: Where the suggestions came from, always shown: "Suggested by AI" in the assistant colour or "Rule-based" in the muted colour.

options.name: onDismiss
options.description: Adds a dismiss button to each action. Remove the action from actions.

options.name: onRun
options.description: Runs an action by id, after approval when it needs it. Running… while it runs, Done when it returns, Failed when it throws.

states.name: running
states.description: Run shows a progress indicator, reads "Running…" and ignores taps.

states.name: done
states.description: Run is replaced by "Done" with a check mark in the strong success colour, the label turns muted, "“…” done." is announced and the success haptic plays.

states.name: failed
states.description: A line in the strong danger colour says "That didn’t work. Try again.", it is announced, the error haptic plays and Run is available again.

states.name: needs approval
states.description: A "Needs approval" tag with a lock; Run opens a system alert titled "Run “…”?" with the description (or the built-in text) and the consequences, a confirm button and Cancel.

states.name: risk
states.description: Medium and high show a warning tag, destructive a danger tag and a confirm button with the destructive role; low shows no tag.

states.name: empty
states.description: "No suggestions right now." under the heading.

appearance: Rows separated by subtle dividers. Labels use the default text colour in the strong body style (muted once done), descriptions the muted caption style; tags are MonarchBadge in the neutral, warning and danger tones; the origin uses the strong assistant colour for AI and the muted text colour for rules; Run is the small secondary Monarch button. All colours are theme roles, so light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow.
platformNotes: The web lays each action out as a row with Run and dismiss at the end; on a phone the buttons go under the text so long labels wrap at the largest text sizes, as on Android. The web's approval is its ConfirmDialog; iOS uses the system alert, which closes when a button is pressed, so a failed run shows its failure line on the row instead of inside the dialog (the web and Android keep the dialog open). The parity map names MonarchAiToolApproval as a dependency, but that component reviews an agent's tool call and its arguments, which a suggested action does not have, so it is not used. The parity map names a list of action rows; the rows are a VStack, not a List, because the list is short and sits on a scrolling record screen, where a List cannot be nested. The risk vocabulary is MonarchAiToolCallRisk, shared with the conversation model. onRun is async throws instead of a returned promise; description and consequences are strings. The origin and dismiss icons are fixed SF Symbols with spoken names, instead of Android's icon slots. The web moves focus to the Done text; on iOS VoiceOver hears the announcement and focus is not moved. The heading level is not offered: VoiceOver has the header trait only. Success and error haptics are added, as iOS apps do for a completed action. Experimental: a product composite that waits for a Rook app to adopt it.
accessibility: The title has the header trait; the origin is a label with text, not only a colour.
Each action's label, description and tags are read as one element.
Run is named "Run “…”" with the action's label; while running it shows a progress indicator and reads "Running…" (MonarchButton's loading state).
Dismiss is an icon button named "Dismiss “…”".
"“…” done." is announced after a run; the failure text is announced after a failed run.
Done and failed are text with a symbol, not only a colour.
Every button is at least 44 points; the approval is the system alert, which VoiceOver focuses.
edgeCases: A controlled status on an action wins over the status the list tracks.
Pressing Run while the action runs or after it is done does nothing.
An empty description falls back to the built-in approval text in the dialog.
Long labels and descriptions wrap; the buttons stay under them.
An empty list shows the empty text under the heading; the origin is still shown.

examples.title: Run, approve and dismiss
examples.code:
MonarchAiSuggestedActions(
    [
        MonarchAiSuggestedAction(
            id: "reminder",
            label: "Send the renewal reminder",
            description: "The contract ends in 14 days and no renewal is recorded."
        ),
        MonarchAiSuggestedAction(
            id: "task",
            label: "Create a follow-up task for next Monday",
            risk: .medium
        ),
        MonarchAiSuggestedAction(
            id: "email",
            label: "Email the account team a status update",
            description: "Goes to 3 people.",
            requiresApproval: true,
            consequences: ["3 people will get an email", "The email is logged on the account"],
            confirmLabel: "Send email"
        ),
        MonarchAiSuggestedAction(
            id: "close",
            label: "Close 4 stale tickets",
            description: "No reply in 60 days.",
            risk: .destructive,
            consequences: ["4 tickets will be closed", "Requesters are notified"],
            confirmLabel: "Close tickets"
        ),
    ],
    onDismiss: { _ in },
    onRun: { _ in }
)
